title: 6 Virtual Assistant Services With No Contracts, Nov 2026
summary: Explore 6 no-contract virtual assistant companies worth trying in November 2026, ranked by pricing, vetting, and flexibility.
body_markdown:
The idea of hiring a virtual assistant is great until you look at the contract. Some services only give you their lowest rate if you commit for 6 or 12 months (MyOutDesk works this way, covered below). If your workload changes faster than that, a long-term commitment becomes a problem. These are the virtual assistant companies with no long-term contracts that give you real flexibility without sacrificing quality.


**TLDR:**


- No-contract VA companies handle recruiting, vetting, and management while you keep the freedom to cancel anytime.
- Compare the full cost, including hour caps, rollover rules and notice periods, along with the hourly rate.
- The services on this list differ in hours, assistant location and how involved they stay after placement.
- MyOutDesk and Wishup fit buyers who want a full-time offshore assistant with an account manager. Zirtual and Time Etc fit buyers who want US-based help for a set number of hours each month.
- Magic fits founders and growing teams that want a full-time Executive Assistant from the top 0.5% of applicants, with regular one-on-ones, and Magic 24/7 included on full-time Executive Assistant plans.


## What Are Virtual Assistant Companies With No Long-Term Contracts?


Virtual assistant companies with no long-term contracts are managed services where you pay for support on a flexible, month-to-month basis. Cancel anytime. Scale up or down as your workload changes. No annual commitments, no early termination fees.


If you hire on your own or through a freelance marketplace, you handle recruiting, onboarding, training, and oversight yourself. No-contract VA companies sit in a different category: they handle recruiting, vetting, and management, while you retain the freedom to stop whenever the arrangement stops working.


That flexibility matters most to founders, executives, and growing teams who rely on a[virtual assistant](https://getmagic.com/virtual-assistant/) whose needs change quickly. A startup scaling through a busy quarter has different requirements than the same company three months later. Locking into a year-long contract during that kind of growth can mean overpaying or being stuck with capacity you no longer need.


## How We Ranked These Virtual Assistant Companies


Each company on this list was reviewed using publicly available information, with no firsthand testing conducted. The criteria below drove every placement decision.


- Flexibility of contract terms: whether you can cancel month-to-month or are locked into a minimum commitment
- Quality of assistant vetting: what the screening process looks like and how selective it is
- Breadth of use cases: whether the service covers just admin work or extends to specialized roles like sales, customer support, or bookkeeping
- Speed to hire: how quickly you can get a matched assistant working
- Co-management and support: whether the company stays involved after placement or hands you the assistant and steps back
- Pricing transparency: whether rates are published openly or require a sales call to find out


VA pricing structures vary widely across the industry, which makes direct comparisons tricky. A low hourly rate can look attractive until you factor in setup fees, unused hours, or the absence of any management layer. We weighted transparency heavily for that reason.

## VaVaVirtual


VaVaVirtual is a US-based virtual assistant agency that serves small business owners with US-based assistants.


### What They Offer


- Administrative, customer service, and data entry support
- Bookkeeping, HR, and recruiting help
- Digital marketing and social media support
- Billing based on hours worked, with no long-term commitment


VaVaVirtual fits owners who want US-based help across admin, bookkeeping, and marketing tasks without a long-term commitment. If you want one assistant working 40 hours a week for you, ask VaVaVirtual about full-time availability, since it doesn’t publish plan details.


## MyOutDesk


MyOutDesk places full-time, dedicated virtual assistants, most of them based in the Philippines, with recruiting, payroll, HR and a dedicated account manager built into one monthly rate.


Here is a closer look at what they offer:


- Assistants for admin, customer service, bookkeeping, marketing, inside sales and transaction coordination
- Specialized roles for healthcare, real estate, finance and other regulated industries
- Every placement is full-time (8 hours a day, 5 days a week), with no part-time plans
- SOC 2 audited and HIPAA verified
- Free rematch if the fit isn’t right


Based on[MyOutDesk’s pricing page](https://www.myoutdesk.com/pricing/) as of November 2026, Managed Outsourcing starts at $1,988 a month and Specialized Outsourcing starts at $2,500 a month. According to[Virtual Wizards](https://virtualwizards.io/myoutdesk/) , that $1,988 rate is month-to-month, with lower rates if you commit to 6 or 12 months.


MyOutDesk fits businesses, especially in regulated industries, that want one full-time offshore assistant with compliance controls and an account manager. It’s a different fit if you want part-time hours or a US-based assistant.


## Zirtual


Zirtual provides dedicated US-based virtual assistants on monthly subscription plans, focused on[executive and administrative support](https://getmagic.com/executive-assistant/) for professionals and small teams.


### What They Offer


- A dedicated assistant who lives in the US, is college educated, and is reachable by phone, text, and email
- Monthly plans from $599 for 12 hours up to $1,699 for 45 hours, plus outbound calling, virtual paralegal, and legal assistant plans
- A kickoff delegation strategy call, with delegation strategists supporting your assistant
- No setup fee and no long-term contract


Based on[Zirtual’s pricing page](https://www.zirtual.com/plans-pricing/) as of November 2026, unused hours don’t roll over, and cancellations take effect the following month. Zirtual fits professionals who want US-based help for a set number of hours each month. If you need someone working 40 hours a week, a full-time service will be a closer fit.


## Wishup


Wishup is a virtual assistant service offering both India-based and US-based assistants, with an emphasis on pre-trained support across a wide range of tools and software.


### What They Offer


- Offshore assistants, including India-based staff working US hours, and US-based assistants
- Assistants trained on 150+ AI and no-code tools, with 8 weeks of training
- Onboarding in as little as 60 minutes
- A dedicated VA manager on every plan, plus a backup VA and customer success manager on the Elite plan
- Separate bookkeeping and automation specialist plans


Based on[Wishup’s pricing page](https://www.wishup.co/pricing) as of November 2026, the full-time Prime plan is $1,999 a month, Elite is $2,999 a month, and a full-time US-based assistant is $5,400 a month, with discounts on annual plans. Wishup advertises cancel anytime.


Wishup fits startups that want a full-time assistant trained on specific tools and onboarded fast. Magic is a different fit if you want regular one-on-ones for your assistant, with Magic 24/7 included on full-time Executive Assistant plans for work that comes up while your assistant is offline.


## Time Etc


Time Etc is a virtual assistant service offering dedicated US-based assistants on prepaid hour bundles, primarily serving entrepreneurs and busy professionals with ongoing admin work.


### What They Offer


- A dedicated US-based assistant, with extra assistants and team sharing at no added cost
- Monthly plans from $390 for 10 hours to $2,160 for 60 hours, with bigger plans on request
- Unused hours roll over on the 20-, 40- and 60-hour plans
- A dedicated Client Happiness manager and built-in holiday and sickness cover


Based on[Time Etc’s pricing page](https://www.timeetc.com/plans-and-pricing) as of November 2026, you can switch plans or cancel any time. Time Etc fits entrepreneurs who want a US-based assistant for a set number of hours a month and pay only for time worked. If you want one person working 40 hours a week for you, a full-time service fits better.

## Why Magic Is the Best Virtual Assistant Company With No Long-Term Contracts


Magic fits founders and growing teams that want a full-time Executive Assistant, picked from the top 0.5% of applicants through live interviews, with regular one-on-ones after placement. Full-time Executive Assistant plans (10 hours a week) include Magic 24/7 coverage for when your assistant is offline. Other services on this list fit different buyers, such as US-based hourly help or a full-time offshore placement.


The cancel-anytime terms remove the financial risk that usually comes with committing to a dedicated assistant. You get full-time, co-managed support without a long-term contract holding you in place if your needs change, so you can[get your Magic assistant](https://getmagic.com/get-your-magic-assistant/) with confidence.


## Final Thoughts on No Long-Term Contract Virtual Assistant Services


The companies on this list all remove the contract risk, but they differ a lot in what you actually get for your money. Some cover admin basics on an hourly basis, others provide full-time co-managed support with backup coverage built in. Knowing what your workload needs week to week makes the right choice pretty clear.


**How do I choose between Magic, Wishup, Zirtual, and the other VA companies on this list?**


Start with how many hours you need and where you want your assistant based. For a full-time assistant, compare Magic, MyOutDesk, and Wishup. Magic adds regular one-on-ones, plus Magic 24/7 on full-time Executive Assistant plans, MyOutDesk adds compliance controls for regulated industries, and Wishup adds tool training and fast onboarding. For US-based help on a set number of hours, Zirtual and Time Etc fit. VaVaVirtual fits owners who want US-based help across admin, bookkeeping, and marketing.


**How does Magic compare with MyOutDesk?**


Both place full-time, dedicated assistants. MyOutDesk focuses on offshore placements with SOC 2 and HIPAA controls, a dedicated account manager, and plans from $1,988 a month as of November 2026. Magic plans start at $360 a week for a Virtual Assistant and $540 a week for an Executive Assistant, with regular one-on-ones on every plan and Magic 24/7 coverage included on full-time Executive Assistant plans (10 hours a week).


**When should I choose a part-time hour-bundle service like Time Etc over a full-time option like Magic?**


Time Etc fits if you want a US-based assistant for a set number of hours each month, from 10 to 60 hours on its published plans as of November 2026. If you want one person working 40 hours a week on your business, a full-time option like Magic fits better.


**What should I look for in a no-contract VA company beyond just the ability to cancel anytime?**


Cancel-anytime terms are a good start, but here are some other things to consider when choosing a virtual assistant service. Look at what happens after placement: does the agency stay involved in managing the assistant, or do you take that over? Also check for backup coverage, how assistants are vetted, and whether pricing is published upfront or requires a sales call.


**Is Wishup or Magic the stronger choice for a startup that needs tool-savvy administrative support?**


Both offer full-time assistants. Wishup fits if you want an assistant trained on 150+ AI and no-code tools, onboarded in as little as 60 minutes, with a dedicated VA manager. Magic fits if you want an Executive Assistant from the top 0.5% of applicants with regular one-on-ones, at $540 a week, with Magic 24/7 coverage included on full-time Executive Assistant plans.


**Can I hire a virtual assistant month-to-month without signing a year-long deal?**


Yes. Magic, VaVaVirtual, Zirtual and Time Etc all let you pay month-to-month with no annual commitment. MyOutDesk and Wishup also offer month-to-month options, though both quote lower rates if you lock in a 6 or 12-month term.


**What happens to unused hours if I pick an hour-bundle VA plan instead of a full-time assistant?**


It depends on the company. Zirtual’s unused hours don’t roll over, while Time Etc rolls over unused hours on its 20-, 40- and 60-hour plans. A full-time assistant working 40 hours a week on your schedule avoids this question altogether since you’re not tracking a bundle.


**Why do some virtual assistant companies require a 6 or 12-month contract for their best rate?**


Locking you into a longer term lets the company guarantee revenue and spread recruiting and training costs over more months, which is why MyOutDesk’s lowest rate requires a 6 or 12-month commitment. Companies that skip that trade, like Magic, make their money back through retention and referrals instead of lock-in.


**How fast can I get a virtual assistant working for me?**


Speed varies by company. Wishup advertises onboarding in as little as 60 minutes, while Magic has you hop on a short call first so Magic can pick the best assistant for your needs and you can meet them before you decide on a start date.


**Should I pick a US-based assistant or an offshore assistant for my business?**


US-based assistants from companies like Zirtual, Time Etc or VaVaVirtual work in your time zone and share cultural context, which helps with phone calls and client-facing work. Offshore assistants from Magic, MyOutDesk or Wishup often cost less for full-time hours and come from a larger applicant pool, which is how Magic can select Executive Assistants from the top 0.5% of applicants.


**What’s the real difference between a VA agency and a freelance marketplace?**


A freelance marketplace leaves recruiting, onboarding, training and oversight to you. A VA company like Magic handles all of that and keeps coaching your assistant after you hire them, so you manage the relationship instead of running HR.


**Can I switch my assistant if the first match isn’t working out?**


Yes, and most no-contract companies build this in. MyOutDesk offers a free rematch, and Magic gives you a full refund or makes it right if you’re not satisfied in the first 2 weeks, so a bad first match doesn’t cost you money or time.


**Do I need a dedicated account manager, or can I manage my assistant myself?**


That depends on how hands-on you want to be. Companies like MyOutDesk, Wishup and Time Etc assign a dedicated manager to handle issues on your behalf, while Magic pairs every assistant with regular one-on-ones so the assistant keeps improving without you having to manage that process.


**How much does a no-contract virtual assistant cost compared to hiring someone in-house?**


A full-time US executive assistant costs a median of $76,590 a year according to BLS data from May 2025, while Magic’s full-time Executive Assistant plan runs $28,080 a year, a $48,510 gap before benefits and taxes. Other no-contract options like MyOutDesk start around $1,988 a month, so comparing total weekly or monthly cost against an in-house salary shows where the real savings sit.


**What should I do if my workload spikes and I need extra help fast without a new contract?**


Look for a company that lets you add help without renegotiating terms. Magic 24/7 gives full-time Executive Assistant plan holders 10 hours a week of extra human help for urgent work when their main assistant is offline, and Magic Teams lets you add more assistants around your workflow without a separate contract for each one.
